item.title: 2026-09-24 Practice: Tax, Regulatory & Industry: Tax Season for Incorporated Clients Starts Now
item.description: - The small business deduction can shrink fast if a corporate portfolio had a strong year, review AAII with incorporated clients now. - Manitoba's budget didn't touch tax rates but sweetened renter and homeowner credits, and added a land transfer tax anti-avoidance rule for 2027. - Watch for CIRO's fraud alert on fake Research Capital Corporation accounts, forward it to clients who've had unsolicited calls. - Richardson Wealth becomes Nobelia on November 30, same structure, new name, expect client questions. - GIC rates have caught up to bonds and probably aren't dropping soon, worth revisiting cash ladders this month.

item.title: 2026-09-24 Manitoba & Winnipeg: Mayoral Race Set, Curriculum and Health Concerns Swirl
item.description: - Winnipeg's mayoral field is locked at twelve candidates, with Kevin Klein's entry turning what looked like an easy Gillingham win into a real contest, though polling shows most voters still undecided. - Councillor Russ Wyatt is pressing ahead with his re-election bid despite facing sexual assault charges and calls from labour leaders and colleagues to step aside. - Manitoba's new health curriculum keeps a parental opt-out for sensitive lessons, a compromise that has pleased some but disappointed educators who wanted a bolder approach. - Health Canada has suspended a Winnipeg plasma clinic's licence following a donor's death, while the former University of Manitoba law dean's arrest in Europe moves a major fraud case closer to a Canadian courtroom.

item.title: 2026-09-24 Canadian Politics: Poilievre Caucus Regroups Amid Trump Tensions and BC Vote
item.description: - Conservative caucus faces internal strain over how firmly to confront Trump on trade threats, with Jason Kenney publicly breaking ranks. - Trump's rhetoric on Canadian immigration and trade continues to shape domestic political debate ahead of the fall sitting. - BC's snap election adds a provincial flashpoint tied directly to the ongoing Canada-US trade conflict. - Carney government pushes ahead on major projects legislation and labour code reform while managing diplomacy in New York. - Defence policy signals a deliberate distancing from Washington, alongside preparations for even remote worst-case scenarios.

item.title: 2026-09-24 Climate Policy & Nonprofit Governance: Ottawa's Bill C-39 Meets Manitoba Energy and Charity Rules
item.description: - Bill C-39 is Ottawa's main tool for fast-tracking energy and infrastructure permits, worth tracking for project timelines. - Alberta's caribou land use plans still favor oil and gas development over habitat recovery goals, say experts. - Okanagan wineries face wildfire damage plus a trade war, a double hit worth knowing for BC-exposed clients. - Manitoba Hydro's new resource plan leans on gas turbines and wind, with critics flagging thin battery storage investment. - CRA no longer pre-approves charity purpose changes, so any client's foundation should get its governance reviewed this year.

item.title: 2026-09-24 AI & Technology: Meta Goes All In On Muse At Connect
item.description: - One, Meta is pushing Muse into hardware, wearables and glasses, showing it sees the AI agent as central to its future rather than a side feature. - Two, Walmart's early but rocky experience with OpenAI's Instant Checkout may still make it a likely partner for Meta's Muse, according to Stratechery's analysis. - Three, the long term contest over agentic shopping could quietly reshape competition between Amazon, Walmart and Meta. - Four, major platforms including YouTube, Spotify and ChatGPT are racing to add conversational and agentic AI features for everyday users. - Five, the US government's rejection of global AI safety standards puts it at odds with leading AI labs pushing for coordinated oversight.

item.title: 2026-09-24 Health & Fitness: Law Sentencing, Cancer Gift, and Tendon Science
item.description: - Princess Margaret Cancer Foundation just landed a hundred million dollar anonymous gift, the largest in its history. - Sentencing began for Kenneth Law in Ontario, a stark reminder of how online sales of lethal chemicals evaded regulators for years. - Manaslu's climbing season ended early after a deadly avalanche killed four, worth flagging for any client planning a Himalayan trip. - New tendon research says there's no single best rep range or exercise, training needs to be personalized. - Outside magazine says a few genuinely affordable climbing towns still exist, if anyone's weighing a lifestyle move.

item.title: 2026-09-24 Parenting: Pregnancy Infections, Sleep Science, and New Parent Benefits
item.description: - Rare pregnancy infections triple autism risk, but standard prenatal screening already catches most cases. - Large sleep study links more REM and deep sleep to lower risk of dozens of diseases, reinforcing paediatric sleep advice. - Custody advice column: document concerns calmly, don't put a teenager in the middle. - EI parental benefits now pay up to 729 dollars a week standard, 437 dollars extended, shareable between parents. - Canada Child Benefit rose in July to 8,157 dollars per child under six, useful for new-parent cash flow planning.

item.title: 2026-09-23 Lessons: Discounted cash flow: the mechanics in five inputs / Pension income splitting and the pension credit / Causal chaining: making one idea lead to the next so the listener cannot stop
item.description: - Company & Economy Analysis: Take one company you know well, pull trailing twelve month free cash flow from Thomson ONE, and run the terminal value calculation twice, once at 2 percent growth and once at 3 percent. Write down the dollar difference in enterprise value between the two. - Financial Planning Facts: Pull last year's tax return for a client over 65 who has RIF income, check line for the pension income amount, and confirm whether form T1032 was actually filed to split income with their spouse. - Communication: Rewrite one recent explanation from a string of "and" sentences into the and, but, therefore structure, and say the new version out loud once.

item.title: 2026-09-23 Markets & Economy: Macklem's Tariff Warning Shadows Rate Path
item.description: - Macklem warns Q4 growth could be halved by US tariffs, below one per cent. - Bank of Canada holds at 2.25 percent, next decision October 28, watch list item. - TSX and Nasdaq both rallied on renewed AI trade led by Meta and Shopify. - Oil dropped over 4 percent on Saudi pipeline and Iran Hormuz signals, easing inflation risk. - Loonie near seven week low despite Macklem's firmer inflation tone, watch the yield spread story.

item.title: 2026-09-23 The Ten: Telesat, Capital Power, Anthropic Lead Business News
item.description: - Telesat's creditor fight is a test of whether Ottawa's flagship tech bet can actually pay its bills. - Capital Power shows the AI data centre boom is now a live political fight over Alberta power rates. - Anthropic's cheaper Claude model means the AI price war is squeezing everyone's margins, not just OpenAI's. - LVMH down 37 per cent this year is the clearest sign the luxury slowdown isn't over yet. - Pickering going offline means Ontario households should expect gas plants, and higher bills, to pick up the slack.

item.title: 2026-09-23 Practice: Tax, Regulatory & Industry: CIRO's Big Fines, Ottawa's New Deduction, Manitoba's Grocery Tax Cut
item.description: - Ask incorporated clients if they have capital purchases planned, the new federal expensing deduction may change the timing. - CIRO handed out 7.6 million in fines to individuals and 8.6 million to firms this year, compliance conversations matter more now. - Manitoba's grocery and prenatal vitamin sales tax relief has been in effect since July, worth confirming clients know. - Gen Z clients are getting defrauded at twice the national rate, raise payment security with younger family members. - Richardson Wealth becomes Nobelia Wealth on November 30th, flag it before clients notice the name change themselves.

item.title: 2026-09-23 Manitoba & Winnipeg: Deficit Halves, Wyatt Runs, Dynacare Ruling Looms
item.description: - Manitoba's deficit came in at 832 million, half what was forecast, and the province says it's on track to balance next year. - Three men wrongfully convicted in 1973 got four million each from the province, plus a separate seven million from the city. - Dynacare's essential services ruling lands by October 1st, and it could reshape strike rights for lab workers province wide. - Twelve names are now on the Winnipeg mayoral ballot, with Gillingham pitching a Main Street revitalization plan. - Manitoba Hydro board members are touring First Nations this week to talk past development damage, reconciliation costs are still live.

item.title: 2026-09-23 Canadian Politics: Carney's Fall Fights and the Prairie Angle
item.description: - Bill C-39 is the big one this fall, it touches project approvals and the right to strike together. - Carney is betting his 46 percent polling number gives him room that Harper never had at similar bills. - Ottawa's 15 percent Trans Mountain equity offer to First Nations is the template for buying in on future corridors. - A new EY study says processing more crops at home could add over 5 billion dollars in GDP, that's a prairie story. - BC's October 24th election is being framed entirely around who can stand up to Trump.

item.title: 2026-09-23 Health & Fitness: Pregnancy Training Science, Wearables, and Rescue Tech
item.description: - Pregnancy training guidelines may loosen, but the underlying studies are still small. - Achilles and calf pain responds better to loaded holds than passive stretching. - New Apple Watch claims best in class heart rate accuracy, independent testers are half convinced. - A Calgary dispatch review found real delays in the Parker Wells search. - Atlantic Canada's air ambulance service quietly takes pressure off rural hospitals.

item.title: 2026-09-23 Parenting: Coffee, Sleep Science, and a Father-Son Road Trip
item.description: - Caffeine can quietly blunt deep sleep even when you feel rested, ask clients with young kids how they are actually sleeping, not just how long. - Teen caffeine use tracks with later bedtimes and shallower sleep, a plain fact for the dinner table. - A structured, budget-first family trip can outperform an expensive one for memory value. - Ghost posting is now a thing your teenager's feed runs on, worth a passing question at home. - If year end planning is coming up, it is a good moment to check RESP contribution room alongside other family goals.

item.title: 2026-09-23 Sports: Jets Fall in OT, Bombers Prep, Kawhi Re-Ups
item.description: - Hellebuyck has reportedly asked the Jets for a trade, that's the story to watch, not the preseason score. - Bombers host Toronto Friday with Collaros still out and Brown getting the practice reps. - NHL board of governors talked Houston and Austin expansion, no decision yet. - Kawhi Leonard just signed two years and 115 million with the Raptors. - Jaxson Dart's knee injury has the Giants worried, Jameis Winston starts in his place.
